title: Rupa's chart of devotion's feelings
hookLine: before the swim, a chart: what each side of Rupa's ocean holds, tears and laughter included
carry: bhakti's rasas: every feeling turned toward krishna
tomorrow: the highest love, in two lines. what does it leave out?

cards: Map apps show the whole route before the first turn. Rupa does the same. Before diving into any single wave, he lays out what each side of his ocean holds.
Read as a list, it's startling. Practice and love, yes. But also tears, trembling, laughter, wonder, even anger and fear.
A book of devotion that maps feelings as carefully as a director plans a play.

teach.b: Here's the chart, side by side. The eastern side is devotion itself, and its waves move in steps: sadhana, the practice anyone can begin; then bhava, the first real stirring of feeling; then prema, love.
The southern side holds what makes a taste: the one who is loved, the setting, the signs that show in the body, like tears or trembling, and the feelings that come and go.
The western side holds the main tastes of loving Krishna: a peaceful love, and love as a servant, a friend, a parent, a beloved. If that sounds familiar, it should.
It's close to the ladder Ramananda climbed by the Godavari, now set down in order by Chaitanya's student.
The northern side holds the tastes that join in along the way: laughter, wonder, heroism, compassion, anger, fear, even disgust. Notice what this chart says about bhakti.
It doesn't ask a devotee to flatten their feelings.
It takes every one seriously enough to map. In Rupa's teaching, a feeling becomes rasa when it's turned toward Krishna.
That's why a grandmother can weep at kirtan, and why on Janmashtami families rock baby Krishna's cradle: love as a parent is one of the main tastes.
Look back at the week: a ladder by a river, a garden with weeds, a ray of the sun, a king's broom, a night of longing, and an ocean with a chart.

how: Gaudiya Vaishnava teachers use the Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu's divisions to explain the stages of devotion and the relationships (rasas) through which devotees love Krishna.

games.q: what does “rupa goswami's bhakti rasamrita sindhu” mean?
o: a book of strict rules for keeping feelings calm
a book that maps devotion's feelings like an ocean
a temple chart of festival days and their duties

s: in Rupa's book, devotion means keeping every feeling calm
his chart maps tears, trembling, laughter, wonder, even anger and fear.
the western side holds love as servant, friend, parent and beloved
close to the ladder Ramananda climbed by the Godavari.
sadhana is the last stage on the chart
sadhana is the practice anyone can begin; then bhava, then prema.

games.q: on Janmashtami, a friend watches your aunt rock a little cradle with baby Krishna in it and asks why she treats God like a baby. by Rupa's chart, what do you say?
o: it's vatsalya, love as a parent: one of the main tastes of loving Krishna.
it's just a game for the kids; adults don't mean it.
it's a mistake; God should only be loved with awe.
games.why: Rupa's western side lists the main tastes of loving Krishna: peaceful, servant, friend, parent, beloved. rocking the cradle is love as a parent.

practice: Rest one hand on your chest, wherever it's comfortable. Notice what taste this moment has: calm, restless, tender, bored.

If you pray, offer that very feeling to Krishna with his name, just as it is: this is what I feel, and it's yours. If you don't pray, name it softly and let it stay under your hand, one more wave on the chart.

wordCard.voice: Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu: an ocean of devotion's tastes, with a chart where tears and laughter both belong.

orig.note: Sanskrit rasa, taste or flavor; Rupa's chart maps devotion's tastes side by side.

carryVoice: The line: bhakti's rasas, every feeling turned toward Krishna. Another week, held.

sources.ref: Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu, the four vibhagas (purva: samanya bhakti, sadhana, bhava, prema; dakshina: vibhava, anubhava, sattvika, vyabhichari and sthayi bhava; pashchima: the main rasas, shanta, dasya, sakhya, vatsalya, madhura; uttara: the secondary rasas, hasya, adbhuta, vira, karuna, raudra, bhayanaka, bibhatsa)
sources.work: Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu of Rupa Goswami (paraphrased)
